questions.question: Build the production cost statement for Mopani Woodworks: raw materials opening R84 000, purchases R612 000, carriage R18 000, closing R90 000; factory wages R390 000 plus employer's contributions R30 000; overheads R296 000 plus sixty percent of R60 000 rent; work-in-progress opening R64 000 and closing R48 000; 24 000 desks finished. Give every level and the unit cost, and state one valid reading of the unit cost falling from last year's R62.
questions.expected_answer: Direct materials issued: 84 000 plus 612 000 plus 18 000 minus 90 000 — R624 000. Direct labour: 390 000 plus 30 000 — R420 000. Prime cost R1 044 000. Factory overheads: 296 000 plus 36 000 — R332 000. Total cost of production R1 376 000; add opening work-in-progress 64 000 and subtract closing 48 000 for cost of production of finished goods of R1 392 000. Unit cost: over 24 000 desks, R58. Valid readings of the fall: variable cost per unit genuinely dropped through better buying or less waste; or fixed overheads were spread over more units, a volume effect rather than efficiency; or quality was cut, which flatters this year and damages the next — the strong answer separates these before praising management.

questions.question: A factory sells mugs at R80 with variable costs of R56 and fixed costs of R432 000; it produced 21 000 mugs this year against 17 500 mugs and a break-even of 17 800 last year. Calculate the break-even point, this year's profit from the margin, the position in both years, and the effect of clay rising R6 a mug.
questions.expected_answer: Contribution: 80 minus 56 is R24. Break-even: 432 000 over 24 — eighteen thousand mugs. This year sits 3 000 mugs beyond the line, so profit is 3 000 times 24 — R72 000, fixed costs being already covered. Last year production of 17 500 fell 300 mugs short of the 17 800 break-even, so the factory made a loss of about R7 200 at last year's contribution; the swing to a 3 000-mug safety margin is the improvement worth naming. Dearer clay thins contribution to R18, lifting break-even to 24 000 mugs — above current production — so management must raise the price, renegotiate supply or cut other variable costs, each with its trade-off stated.

questions.question: March's cash from sales given: sales January R150 000, February R190 000, March R210 000; thirty percent cash; credit collected sixty percent the next month and thirty-five percent the second month with five percent bad. Then settle the VAT: output on R560 000 of exclusive sales, input R61 500, drawings R4 000 excluding VAT, a bad debt of R6 900 inclusive.
questions.expected_answer: March receipts: cash sales thirty percent of 210 000 — R63 000; sixty percent of February's credit sales of 133 000 — R79 800; thirty-five percent of January's credit sales of 105 000 — R36 750; total R179 550, with the five percent bad debts appearing nowhere because no cash moves. VAT: output fifteen percent of 560 000 — R84 000; minus input 61 500 leaves R22 500; drawings return the input claim, adding fifteen percent of 4 000 — R600; the inclusive bad debt reclaims fifteen over one hundred and fifteen of 6 900 — R900 subtracted. Owed to SARS: R22 200, held in trust and never the business's own money.
